# Review Log — go-path-reliability

Per-phase review findings from the `/ship:go` build spine (profile: thorough, review gate on).

## Phase 1 — Verifier durability — helper and contract (round 1)

Status: APPROVED
Verify: 4 re-run — 4 pass, 0 fail, 0 not runnable
Reviewed: 4 file(s)

- [medium] agents/ship-verifier.md:102: The incremental record is a full rewrite, and `tests` is specified as 'array of { file, commit } for every test file you have committed' — first person, current run. The salvage branch (lines 68-73) tells a retry to adopt base_head, criteria verdicts and carried-finding outcomes from the record, but never says the rewritten record must carry the predecessor's tests[] (or criteria) entries forward. A retry reading it literally writes a record listing only its own commits while keeping the inherited base_head, so the dead run's test commits sit inside base_head..HEAD unlisted and verify-scratch.cjs rejects that record on 'foreign commit' at the next validation. The salvage chain therefore breaks after a second consecutive death. Failure direction is safe (reject -> full re-verify), so the cost is a wasted verification, not a wrong result. — recorded
- [low] tests/pm-state-conformance.test.js:199: Not caused by this phase, but relevant to it: the full suite (`node --test` from the repo root) has one failure — dashboard.html rendered from the local gitignored .project-manager/ROADMAP.md is stale relative to a backlog row ('Re-run check against a ship-owned archived feature'). 593 pass, 1 fail. All four of this phase's verify commands pass. Phase 4's acceptance criterion requires the whole suite green. — recorded
- [low] .planning/features/go-path-reliability/PLAN.md:333: Task 12's verify command ends in `node --test tests/`, which errors on this machine's Node (v25.8.1) with 'Cannot find module /Users/dilhan/src/ship/tests' — the directory argument is resolved as a module entrypoint. Bare `node --test` from the repo root works. Task 2's verify names a file and is unaffected. — recorded

## Phase 3 — Transport honesty and depends enforcement (round 1)

Status: NEEDS_FIXES
Verify: 3 re-run — 3 pass, 0 fail, 0 not runnable
Reviewed: 4 file(s)

- [high] ship/workflows/go.workflow.js:745: The verifier-outage INFRASTRUCTURE branch is unreachable in the normal case. safeAgent increments consecutiveTransportDeaths once per *call* (noteDeath runs once, after both attempts), not once per attempt, and any successful agent resets it to 0. The verify call is a single safeAgent call, so a verifier killed by an outage leaves the counter at 1 and `consecutiveTransportDeaths >= MAX_TRANSPORT_RETRIES` (3) is never true unless the two preceding review agents also died on transport. A plain verifier outage therefore still falls through to section 6 item 7 (null verdict, nothing stopped): CONTEXT.md `built` and headless outcome `error` (documented as an unrecoverable skill-level failure) instead of the resumable `infrastructure`. The build path is unaffected — the builder runs with retry:false, so each round contributes one death and the cap works there. — fixed in fix round
- [medium] skills/go/SKILL.md:180: When the verify pseudo-phase sets stoppedAt with INFRASTRUCTURE, section 6 item 5 applies and instructs leaving CONTEXT.md at `building` — but every phase built successfully, so the correct recorded state is `built`, which is exactly what item 7 sets for the same real situation when the transport counter did not trip. The same event yields two different recorded statuses depending on how many consecutive transport deaths preceded it. — recorded
- [low] ship/workflows/go.workflow.js:241: The 5xx pattern /(status|error)[^0-9]{0,20}50\d/i can match a non-transport agent error whose message contains 'error' followed within 20 non-digit characters by a 50x number (e.g. 'error ... at line 501'). A false positive silently un-charges a build round and can end the run as INFRASTRUCTURE with a misleading reason. — recorded
- [low] skills/go/SKILL.md:212: The new INFRASTRUCTURE sentence sits inside the fenced GO COMPLETE template as an indented line with no `[If ...]` marker, unlike every other conditional line in that block. An agent rendering the template literally may emit the meta-instruction into the user-facing report. — recorded
- [low] tests/pm-state-conformance.test.js:199: Pre-existing, not caused by this phase (the phase-3 diff touches no PM files): the suite fails locally because pm-state-conformance asserts the gitignored .project-manager/dashboard.html matches the local ROADMAP.md backlog. Separately, `node --test tests/` (phase 4 task 12's verify command) errors with MODULE_NOT_FOUND on Node 25 and needs `node --test 'tests/*.test.js'`. Both will block phase 4's verify. — recorded

- [medium] tests/pm-state-conformance.test.js:199: The CI-form full-suite run exits 1 on exactly one test: dogfood 'renders the project name, every milestone, and every backlog item from ROADMAP.md', for backlog item "Re-run check against a ship-owned archived feature". Cause is outside this diff: the test strips backticks from the roadmap cell and expects the dashboard to render inline code as <code>, but ship/pm-update.cjs emits the backticks literally into .project-manager/dashboard.html. Neither ship/pm-update.cjs nor that test file is touched by any of the 12 commits in this feature. It only fires on a machine holding local gitignored .project-manager/ state (dashboard regenerated 22 Aug 16:00 by the go run's pm-update step); a clean checkout skips the suite, so the release CI job stays green. Flagged because task 12's verify is billed as the whole-feature integration verify and does not pass locally. — recorded
- [medium] tests/go-path-reliability.test.js:100-104: The assertion `branch.indexOf('consecutiveTransportDeaths >= MAX_TRANSPORT_RETRIES') < branch.indexOf('round -= 1')` passes vacuously when the left string is absent (indexOf returns -1, less than any real index). Confirmed by mutation against a throwaway copy of HEAD: rewriting the guard as `if (false) {` leaves the whole suite green (exit 0), even though a real outage would then decrement `round` forever - the exact infinite loop the plan's Risk Note says this guard prevents. Keying the cap on the wrong variable (e.g. `if (round >= MAX_TRANSPORT_RETRIES)`) would slip through the same way. Deleting the guard block entirely IS caught, via the neighbouring `return {` assertion. The rest of the new assertions mutation-check correctly: reverting ship-verifier maxTurns to 40, dropping `salvaged` from REVIEW_SCHEMA, unescaping one ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, weakening the builder's depends rule, reverting the headless count to 11, and changing the Stage 1 marker inside Stage 1 each fail the suite as intended. — recorded
